subject: Mythology
title: Codices: Books the Spanish Burned
description: A fast breakdown of Codices: Books the Spanish Burned for builders.

hook.text: The Spanish burned thousands of Aztec and Maya books. Only about 20 Mesoamerican codices survive today.

buildup.text: Codices were folding books made from bark paper or deerskin, painted with mythological scenes and calendar records.

discovery.text: Bishop Diego de Landa burned every Maya book he could find, calling them superstition and lies of the devil.

twist.text: Landa felt guilty and wrote a book about Maya culture. Ironically, his book became the key to decoding their writing.

climax.text: The surviving codices are now among the most valuable documents in human history, studied in museums worldwide.

punchline.text: The man who destroyed Maya knowledge accidentally preserved enough to save it.

quiz.question: How did Bishop Diego de Landa accidentally help preserve Maya knowledge?
options: He secretly hid codices in a Spanish monastery
He wrote a book about Maya culture that became key to decoding their writing
He trained Maya scribes to rewrite their stories in Spanish
